review.evidenceBasis: Checked every mapping row of the 34-row draft against the igcse-further-maths-19 (4PM1) spine, per (video,spec). Kept the low rows whose partial support names a clause genuinely in the spec (index rules for 1B's indices half, linear-only solving for 3D 'Simple inequalities, linear and quadratic', cubic/reciprocal for 4A's halves, parallel/perpendicular for 8E's halves, resultants for 7A addition, SOH CAH TOA for 10B's three-basic-ratios head). Rejected 3 spec-level bindings where the evidence concedes the spec's distinctive content is not title-evidenced: sequence-classification off 5B series, degree-measure arc/sector off 10A radian measure, and basic 2D Pythagoras off 10C's 2D/3D applied-problems frame.

rejects.reason: 'Types of Number Sequences - Arithmetic vs Geometric' names sequence-type recognition; 5B is 'Arithmetic and geometric series' — nth-term and sum-of-terms formulae — and the evidence itself concedes 'series sums not named'. Same 'arithmetic/geometric' words, different topic (sequence classification vs series summation); keyword-adjacent, rejected at low. (The same title is correctly kept in the additional-maths lane against 12.3.1, whose distinctive content IS progression recognition.)

'Area of a Sector and Length of an Arc of a Circle (Circles Part 3)' is the degree-measure GCSE treatment; 10A's distinctive content is 'Radian measure, including use for arc length and area of sector' — the radian clause is the head of this spec point and the evidence concedes 'radian measure not named'. Degree-based arc/sector work is not title-evidenced for a radian-measure spec; rejected at low.

'Pythagoras' Theorem And How To Use It' is the basic right-triangle theorem lesson; 10C is 'Applications to simple problems in two or three dimensions (including angles between a line and a plane and between two planes)' — the evidence concedes the 3D plane-angle clause is not named and offers only generic 2D use. Title names a tool, not the spec's applied-problems frame; keyword-adjacent, rejected at low.
